title: From an Address to a Web Page

scenes.purpose: Pose the question and preview the three steps

visual.title: What happens when you press Enter?
visual.statement: A page can appear in a second or two, but several steps happen first.

narration.text: You type a website address, press Enter, and a page appears almost instantly.
Behind that moment, your computer quietly completes a short journey.
First, it has to find the server that holds the page.
Next, it asks that server for the page.
Finally, it turns the reply into what you see.

scenes.purpose: Explain how a name becomes a server address

narration.text: Computers find each other by numbers called IP addresses, not by names.
So your browser first asks a DNS resolver which number belongs to the name you typed.
The resolver answers with an IP address, a bit like a phone book returning a number.

scenes.purpose: Show the request travelling to the server

narration.text: Now the browser opens a connection to that IP address.
Its request travels across the internet in small pieces called packets.
The request reaches the web server and says which page the browser wants.

scenes.purpose: Show the response coming back and the page being drawn

narration.text: The server sends back a response that contains the page, written in a language called HTML.
The browser reads that HTML and fetches any images or styles it mentions.
Then it draws everything on your screen, and the web page appears.

visual.title: The whole journey
visual.statement: Find the server, ask for the page, show the result.
points: Requests and replies travel as packets
The browser builds the page you see

narration.text: So every time you press Enter, three things happen.
DNS turns the name into an IP address.
Your request and the server's reply travel across the internet as packets.
And your browser builds the page you see, often in just a second or two.
